method: Same AI agent reread aligned source and target and produced reverse paraphrases. This is not independent human review or a fluency certification.
scope: All 86 linguistic blocks compared during drafting; nine conceptual-risk blocks explicitly reverse-paraphrased here.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: Two sets are equal exactly when every member of the first belongs to the second and conversely.
samples.comparison: Both directions preserved; no existence claim added to definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors; six is the only positive perfect number below ten, with the displayed source bound 0 <= x <= 10 unchanged.
samples.comparison: Definition and example preserved. Source subsequently qualifies general set-existence wording in Russell section; translation keeps that sequencing. Perfect-number lexical label remains provisional.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: Two belongs to the integers; even numbers form a subset. A set can simultaneously be a member and subset of another set.
samples.comparison: Membership versus inclusion, singleton and nested singleton examples intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: A equals B exactly when each is a subset of the other; the two halves correspond to extensionality.
The intersection of a family contains precisely the objects common to every member of that family.
samples.comparison: Universal scope, not existential. Source's empty-family convention is not silently repaired.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: Triples are nested pairs with the first component a pair; quadruples nest to the left in the same way.
samples.comparison: Wiener–Kuratowski/nesting formulas unchanged; provisional Gujarati tuple labels recorded.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: For each x in A there are m pairs with that first component; distinct first components give disjoint rows, hence n times m members.
samples.comparison: Counting proof preserves disjointness and union argument.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: Extensionality gives uniqueness of the set satisfying a property, if it exists; it does not grant existence for every property.
samples.comparison: Conditional scope explicitly preserved, with existence italicized in target.

samples.reverse_paraphrase_english: Assuming R belongs to itself contradicts its defining nonselfmembership; assuming nonmembership satisfies the defining property and yields membership.
samples.comparison: Both branches retained; no appeal to a universal set or native witness replaces the original proof.

known_language_uncertainty: See TERM_DECISIONS.jsonl; source meaning governs every provisional term.
